title: Connect your sound desk
blurb: Get the cleanest sound into Hearken, from a desk, a microphone or a livestream.
body:
The clearer the sound, the faster and more accurate Hearken is. A direct feed from the desk beats a microphone in the room.

  1. Run a cable from the desk’s aux, record or matrix output into the laptop’s audio input, or into a USB audio adapter.
  2. In Hearken, open the Input menu and pick that input. The list refreshes when you point at it, so devices plugged in later appear.
  3. Ask someone to speak at the pulpit and watch the level meter next to the menu move.
  4. Press Start listening. The first start times your computer and picks the right speed settings.

If the meter barely moves, raise the send on the desk rather than the laptop’s input volume. To listen to the computer’s own audio instead (a livestream feed), choose an input marked 🔁 on Windows, or install BlackHole on a Mac.

title: Put the verses on the projector
blurb: Send the output to a second screen, and black it out or clear it in a hurry.
body:
1. Connect the projector or TV as a second display.
  2. Choose it in the display menu next to Open output, or leave it on Auto to use the second display.
  3. Click Open output. It fills that screen; press Esc on it to close it.
  4. Use Black (B) to black out the screen and Clear (Esc) to remove the verse. Verse ▶ steps to the next verse.

On a laptop with no projector attached, the output opens as an ordinary window so you can rehearse.

title: Add a lower third in OBS or vMix
blurb: Show each verse over your livestream as a clean caption.
body:
1. Click Share and switch on sharing on the local network.
  2. Copy the livestream overlay address, for example http://hearken.local/overlay.
  3. In OBS, add a Browser source, set it to 1920 × 1080 and paste the address. In vMix, add a Web Browser input.
  4. Each verse now appears as a caption at the bottom. Add ?pos=top to the address to move it to the top.

Using a hardware video switcher? Open Screens, add a Lower third screen on green or black, and key it out on the switcher.

title: Run the screen from your phone
blurb: Next verse, black screen and show any detection, from anywhere in the room.
body:
The phone remote lets a pastor, worship leader or second volunteer move the screen on from anywhere in the room.

  1. Click Share on the media desk and switch on sharing. The phone must be on the same Wi‑Fi as the laptop.
  2. Open the Remote address shown in the Share panel, for example http://hearken.local/remote, on the phone.
  3. Enter the 4-digit PIN shown in the Share panel. It changes each time Hearken starts.
  4. Use Previous and Next to step through verses, Black to black out the screen and Clear to remove the verse.
  5. Below the buttons are the latest detections and the sermon plan. Tap Show on any of them to put it on screen.

The media desk stays in charge: anything sent from the remote also appears on the dashboard’s Live screen, and the operator can change it at any time.

title: Let members follow on their phones
blurb: A QR code on the screen, any translation and text size, and the recap after service.
body:
1. Click Share and switch on sharing. Phones must be on the same Wi‑Fi as the laptop.
  2. Click Show QR on screen. A code appears in the corner of the projector.
  3. Members scan it and see the live verse. They can choose any translation and make the text bigger.
  4. After the sermon, the Recap button on their phone opens the scriptures, songs and sermon notes, with PDF and Word downloads.

Some Android phones can’t open .local addresses. The QR code always works.

title: Add Yoruba, Igbo or Hausa Bibles
blurb: Download a translation and show it on its own or side by side.
body:
1. Click ＋ Bibles in the top bar.
  2. Click Download next to the translation you want. Each is about 4–5 MB and takes a few seconds.
  3. Choose it under Translation to show it on its own, or under Side by side to show it next to English.

Once downloaded, translations work offline and appear on members’ phones too, with book names in their own language.

title: Import your worship songs
blurb: Lyrics that follow the singers, and a usage report for your CCLI licence.
body:
1. Open the Songs tab.
  2. Paste the lyrics: the title on the first line, then each part separated by a blank line. You can head parts “Verse 1”, “Chorus” and so on. Or import .txt files.
  3. Make sure Lyrics is switched on in the top bar.
  4. While you listen, the song being sung shows up as a card, and its sections follow the singers.

Hearken includes no lyrics. Import only songs your church is licensed to project. The CCLI report at the bottom of the Songs tab lists what you used.
